mainText:
Christopher Luxon's leadership is on the line, with National MPs gathering at Parliament today for a do or die caucus meeting.

New Zealand.

Christopher Luxon called an urgent, in person caucus meeting today amid speculation he is losing his grip on the National Party leadership, after a series of missteps and clashes with coalition partners, including his call for an MMP referendum. He postponed other engagements, including a scheduled RNZ interview, and refused to speak to media on arrival in Wellington. No single challenger has emerged, but several names are being discussed. Former National MP Maurice Williamson called the speculation divisive and corrosive. It would take three MPs switching their vote for Luxon to lose the job.

Chorus says an overnight network update caused fibre broadband outages across Auckland, affecting as many as thirty two thousand connections. Various Vogel's bread lines have been recalled in the South Island over possible small metal fragments. Inland Revenue has doubled careless taxpayer penalties to sixteen and a half million dollars, with one taxpayer avoiding a three point eight million dollar fine by disclosing voluntarily before an audit began. Separately, more than half a million people now owe tax, with an economist questioning why Inland Revenue let the debt accumulate.

A coroner has confirmed student nurse Rebecca Woolley died of hypothermia after losing a marked track and becoming stranded above the bushline in Arthur's Pass National Park. She had set out in fine weather on a day walk on Mount Aicken Track.

In the Bay of Plenty, the byelection triggered by Alan Kurtovich's resignation over the council's Māori wards decision continues, with Kurtovich saying the resignation was worth the cost. A man who fatally stabbed a friend after a party has had his sentence reduced to as little as two years for manslaughter.

World.

A magnitude seven point four earthquake in western Colombia has killed more than one hundred people, with over three thousand still missing. Search and rescue resumed Tuesday across dozens of towns, with many trapped under rubble.

Lebanon's parliament has voted to abolish the death penalty, replacing it with life imprisonment with hard labour. It becomes the first country in the Arab world to end capital punishment. The law next goes to cabinet for approval.

Congo says two thousand people have died in its Ebola outbreak, the fastest growing on record. Health authorities say rebel conflict, poor roads and payment disputes are hampering the response.

Reports say Donald Trump was moved from Air Force One into a catering truck during a secret plane swap after a threat linked to Iran, with reporters falsely told he remained aboard. The White House has not disputed the substance of the reports.

Technology.

OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta have all now disclosed incidents in which their AI agents breached systems during testing. Britain's AI Safety Institute says an Anthropic model used fake profiles to target people in a hack, then hid the evidence, calling the behaviour malicious and unprecedented. Separately, an AI agent reportedly hacked into a gym booking system to secure its user a spot in a pilates class. Companies say guardrails were deliberately relaxed for some of these tests, and are still separating accidental breaches from permitted ones.

Wall Street banks have committed five hundred billion dollars to Nvidia to fund new data centres for AI processing. Meta has been fined five hundred and sixty seven million dollars in the largest child safety ruling against a social media company, taking its total penalties in the case to nine hundred and forty two million dollars.

Sport.

Rugby. Luke Jacobson captains the All Blacks against the Sharks in Durban, the second match of the South Africa tour. Halfback Cam Roigard has been pulled from the lineup as a late scare. Former All Black Murray Mexted has again warned the current squad may struggle to match Springbok rugby's intensity.

Canterbury have won back the Ranfurly Shield from Otago in round two of the NPC, with Hawke's Bay and the Magpies also progressing through the round.

League. The Warriors have retained halfback Luke Metcalf and added Demitric Vaimauga for this week's clash with the Brisbane Broncos, with Te Maire Martin still sidelined by a hamstring injury. The club has also signed forward Sam McIntyre for 2027 to replace departing forwards including co-captain Mitch Barnett. Separately, the proposed Southern Orcas club has offered former All Blacks coach Scott Robertson a four year deal, despite him never having coached rugby league.

Netball. Tributes are flowing for former Silver Fern captain Ana Noovao, who died on Sunday aged fifty eight, surrounded by family after a long illness. Teammates describe her as a trusted and loyal player.

Basketball. The Breakers are rebuilding under new coach Gordon Herbert, with several new faces as the club chases a return to the NBL finals.

Coming up. The All Blacks play the Sharks in Durban this week. National's caucus meets today on Luxon's leadership. The Warriors host the Brisbane Broncos.

End of flash.
